front_line: A modern beauty company built for the social media era
thesis: I owned e.l.f. because it turns TikTok trends into cash flow, winning beauty with speed rather than volume at prices that hold up in tough times. I closed it because the thesis realized faster than the fundamentals, running +63.2% versus the S&P in just 73 days on Rhode outperformance and tariff relief. With the stock back near 30x FY27 adjusted EPS, the forward asymmetry compressed. I would revisit if core organic growth reaccelerates.
moat: Genuine low-cost-producer edge, but rented shelves and rented attention cap it at narrow.
risks: Earnings beats shrinking quarter over quarter (+70% → +18% → +11%).

lifecycle.open_note: ELF is the beauty brand that moves at internet speed. Turning TikTok trends into cash flow, and winning beauty with speed- not volume. Trend-driven categories can cool quickly, but ELF has established its brand relevance as well as its moat- speed, consumer data, marketing execution, and distribution. ELF's management has an exceptional understanding of social media and influcer-driven demand. At affordable prices this creates resilience in tougher economic enviornments.
lifecycle.close_note: Thesis realized faster than fundamentals. Rhode outperformance and tariff relief helped drive outperformance versus the S&P 500 in just 73 days at +63.2%, while core organic growth still faces a reacceleration test. With valuation back near 30x FY27 adjusted EPS, I closed the position as forward asymmetry compressed.

drafts.x_post: $ELF is misread by both the mania crowd and the bears. The gap between net income and free cash flow isn't decay — it's growth, money plowed back into inventory to fund expansion. Low-cost producer in a price-driven category, at a normal price. Dead Simple Score: 92.
video_talking_points: e.l.f. makes cheap, on-trend makeup, skincare, and now hair care for younger shoppers.
It's beaten earnings four quarters running and is now expanding into hair care and overseas.
The bull point: it's the low-cost producer in a category where price is the weapon — a $6 product that looks like a $40 one.
The main risk: the whole thesis rests on growth not slowing, and the beats are already shrinking.
The verdict: buy as a small satellite — clean asymmetry with a kill-switch on a known earnings date.
